entries.description: Register.

**Re-derive this repo's three suites against the stronger definition of `covers`,** and fix what it exposes. Every prefix that can change a suite's result must be declared — including the ones the old reading let sit outside, such as build and test configuration and lockfiles. Report what moved and what deliberately did not; a declaration this set does not change is a *finding*, not a silence.

**Ship `affected_suites()` and make suite loading fail closed.** `affected_suites(files_changed, suites)` returns which suites a change set affects **and which inputs matched**, and `evaluate_freshness()` consumes it rather than re-deriving per suite (one definition — L-069-1). `load_suites()` gains a checked result carrying its errors, and `check_test_run_fresh()` **blocks** on a suite-configuration error instead of reading it as "no expensive suites".

**Falsify in both directions** (`L-112-1`), by planting the declaration rather than reading the code. FIRES: one shared input affects several suites; an input changed after a run stales it; a malformed `testing.suites` block **blocks the close** rather than disarming the gate; an empty declaration cannot pass as "nothing owed". DOES NOT FIRE: an input touched by no suite owes nothing; a repo with no `docs/modules.yaml` behaves exactly as it does today. STRUCTURAL: the reported `changed_inputs` for a real change set equals the intersection an independent walk computes.
**Cross-provider verification.**
**Required portion of the full test suite.**
**Close-out.**
Registered session 1 (github-copilot / claude-opus-5, high).

Re-derived all three suites against the stronger definition of covers. Derivation was EMPIRICAL: a full pytest run under a sys.addaudithook tracer recorded every repo path the suite opened or enumerated (1655 distinct). Added to pytest: pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, .github/, test-fixtures/, scripts/, tests/, docs/templates/, tools/dabbler-ai-orchestration/dist/templates/, tools/dabbler-ai-orchestration/changelog.d/. Added to mocha: package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json (test:unit = mocha via ts-node). Added to playwright: esbuild.js, tsconfig.json, playwright.config.ts, package-lock.json (test:playwright = npm run compile && npx tsc && npx playwright test). Deliberately NOT declared, with reasons recorded in the module docstring: docs/session-sets/ (the gate own bookkeeping lives there; record_run digests then appends test-runs.jsonl, so the suite would stale its own run - demonstrated, reports PREDATES with nothing else touched) and docs/planning/ (cite_lessons rewrites lesson trailers in the final commit, after the run of record). MANIFEST.in looked like an input and the trace never touched it - correctly absent.

Shipped affected_suites(files_changed, suites) -> tuple[SuiteMatch] reporting suite, changed_inputs and matched_prefixes; evaluate_freshness now consumes it once instead of re-deriving per suite (L-069-1) and FreshnessVerdict carries changed_inputs. Unified four copies of prefix matching into matching_prefixes(); that unification exposed and fixed a live bug - session_touched normalised with lstrip('./'), a CHARACTER-set strip that ate the leading dot of every dotfile, so .github/ and .gitignore declarations matched nothing while reading as correct (fail-open). Added load_suites_checked() -> SuiteLoadResult(suites, errors); load_suites() is now its error-discarding projection. check_test_run_fresh blocks on a suite-configuration error instead of reading zero suites as no expensive suites. CLI: new affected subcommand, check prints matched inputs and refuses a malformed declaration.

Ten new test functions in ai_router/tests/test_run_of_record_affected_suites.py, on the declared irony budget, weighted to fail-closed. FIRES: shared input fans out to several suites and names what matched; a build-config input changed after a run stales it (PREDATES); six plausible typo shapes are reported instead of dropped; a non-list suites: key no longer silently becomes DEFAULT_SUITES; the close gate blocks on a malformed declaration; an empty declaration cannot pass as nothing owed. DOES NOT FIRE: an input under no declared input set owes nothing; an explicit suites: [] stays the deliberate operator disarm; affected_suites is identical with and without a docs/modules.yaml assigning the path to a different module (A5, structurally). STRUCTURAL: changed_inputs equals an intersection recomputed by ancestor-set membership rather than startswith, with both the change set and the suite corpus asserted non-empty (L-112-1). Plus a falsifier for the dotfile bug.

Five rounds, verifier gpt-5.5 (openai) on every one -- a different effective provider from the orchestrator, enforced by registry-resolved exclusion. Discovery fan-out 2 (spec-conformance, failure-scenario) -> 5 Major; supplementary -> 1 Major; remediation-review -> 1 Major; remediation-review cycle 2 -> 2 Major; operator-authorized round 5 -> VERIFIED, 0 findings, 8 fixes accepted + 1 accepted-with-modification. Nine Major findings total, all accepted, none disputed, all fixed. Round 5 needed the operator attestation because cycles 1-2 were spent settling earlier rounds fixes, leaving round 4 two findings fixed but unreviewed. Verification earned its cost: it caught that Layer 2 and Layer 3 had been derived from their COMMANDS rather than from what their specs read, and then caught a narrowing this session had recorded as a deliberate decision on a FALSE premise -- Layer 3 does not exercise the published router, it pip install -e s this tree.

All three suites owed and all three run after the last code change. pytest: 4349 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed (713.4s). mocha: 1450 passing, 2 pending, 0 failing (187.7s). playwright: 31 passed, 0 failed (374.6s) at --workers=2, CI worker count. The first full playwright pass at the 4-worker local default starved the Electron launches and timed out vsix-first-run-walkthrough at 0 sets; the spec passes in isolation in 53.9s and the re-run at CI worker count is 31/31, matching Sets 123/124/127/128 exactly -- the parallel-load flake Set 122 recorded on this box, not a regression. All three recorded as runs of record. Note the obligation itself is this session own deliverable: mocha and playwright were owed only because this session declared ai_router/ an input of both, which is the change under test dogfooding itself.
Register.

**Write A5's answer and the corrected safety claim into the authoring guide,** beside A1–A4 where an author already looks: the suite declares its inputs, the intersection decides the obligation, modules group. Carry the replacement wording for the "provably redundant" claim verbatim, and say plainly why the stronger version is refused — it would let a skip happen without the operator attestation that a verification reduction requires.

**Record the refusals so they are not re-proposed,** and retire the question. Eight rejections with their reasons and six deferrals with their **trigger conditions** (`verdict.md` §6–§7) land where a future author will meet them, not only in a proposal folder. Then close A5 in `docs/planning/session-step-skeleton-and-verification-cost.md` — it is the last open item in that note — and author `change-log.md`.
**Cross-provider verification.**
**Required portion of the full test suite.**
**Close-out**, including the Step 9 reorganization review of `project-guidance.md` / `lessons-learned.md`.
Registered session 2 (github-copilot / claude-opus-5, high).

A5 answered in the authoring guide beside A1-A4, and the section is now A1-A5. Three parts: the suite declares its inputs (covers = the complete input allowlist, derived from EVIDENCE not from the suite command -- S1 traced 1655 paths under an audit hook and its command-derived first draft for Layers 2/3 was the gap verification caught); the intersection decides (run_of_record affected names the suites AND the inputs that matched, evaluate_freshness consumes the same affected_suites so report and gate cannot disagree, L-069-1); modules group and do not select (no SuiteSpec.module, three reasons: the input set already answers it, a module axis can only SUBTRACT and fails open per L-125-1, and the label is unenforced -- no codeRoots-vs-imports check exists, section 6.4). Fail-closed loading written up: a malformed testing.suites block blocks the close; suites: [] stays the deliberate operator disarm. The corrected safety claim carried verbatim from verdict.md 2a, with the reason the stronger 'provably redundant' framing is REFUSED: it would let a skip happen without the operator attestation a verification reduction requires. Stated explicitly that A5 authorizes no new skip. Also updated the two stale echoes: the 'read covers literally' paragraph now names the input-set definition and the suite-key allowlist (name/command/covers/expensive/tests), and the constitution's Step 8 required-portion sentence now says intersection and names the command (preload total 12,183/12,200 tokens, still under ceiling).

Refusals and deferrals recorded, A5 retired, change-log.md authored. The eight rejections (with reasons) and six deferrals (with their TRIGGER conditions, not a schedule) are now two tables in the authoring guide immediately after A5 -- where an author proposing contract locks or module-scoped test selection meets them, not in a proposal folder nobody re-reads. session-step-skeleton-and-verification-cost.md: A5's heading is RESOLVED, its marker answers the three sub-questions in order and names where the canonical text now lives, the note's status header says no open items remain, and verdict.md joins Related work. The note's own convention is honoured -- the 2026-08-12 diagnosis prose is preserved verbatim beneath the inline marker rather than rewritten. module-organized-projects-recommendation.md section 6.4 now carries the rule that the scope check, when built, may never be read as an input to suite selection; that is the one place a future author would most plausibly reintroduce the module axis, and the section's own admission that no codeRoots-vs-imports check exists is the argument. Authored change-log.md (both sessions, what was refused and why, what deliberately did not change) and ai_router/changelog.d/0110-set-129-suite-owned-input-sets.md as a FRAGMENT rather than an edit to the shared CHANGELOG; changelog check --target all round-trips OK.

One round, VERIFIED, 0 findings. Discovery fan-out 2 (lenses spec-conformance and failure-scenario), verifier gpt-5.5 (openai) on both calls -- a different effective provider from the orchestrator, enforced by the registry-resolved exclusion (excluded providers: anthropic). Both lenses checked the A5 doctrine against verdict.md, the guide, the diagnosis note, the module recommendation, the constitution echo, the changelog fragment, the set change log and the drift-guard test change, and both reported the refusals, deferrals, corrected claim and current-code behaviour claims consistent. Per A1/A2 only TARGETED tests preceded this: test_guidance_preload_manifest, test_guidance_meta, test_guidance_report, test_changelog_partition, test_drift_guard, test_doc_only_cap, test_step_status_drift. That targeted run caught a real defect this session CAUSED: test_changelog_round_trip_flags_a_planted_reorder planted its reorder into load_fragments()[0:2] -- the two NEWEST fragments -- while changelog.check() deliberately re-renders from the BASELINE set alone, so the falsifier only fired while at most one post-baseline fragment existed. This set's own fragment made it two and the plant stopped firing. Fixed test-only: it now selects from the baseline corpus and asserts that corpus is non-empty (L-112-1), matching the baseline_fragments() helper in test_changelog_partition.py whose docstring names this exact hazard and which the drift-guard copy had not used (L-069-1). The gate itself was never wrong. New deliverables were git-added before the evidence bundle so the diff-based evidence does not omit them (L-064-9).

All three suites owed and all three run after the last code change, then recorded; run_of_record check reports all three fresh and green. pytest: 4349 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed (681.4s). mocha: 1455 passing, 2 pending, 0 failing (47.9s). playwright: 31 passed, 0 failed (399.2s) at --workers=2, the CI worker count that Sets 122/123/124/127/128 all use on this box. The mocha count moved from Session 1's 1450 to 1455 legitimately: commit d6b99264, an ad-hoc operator fix landed between the two sessions, added workExplorerTreeModel tests. Layer 3 is 31 in both sessions. The obligation was resolved with the set's own tool rather than by eye -- run_of_record affected named all three suites and, in every case, the SAME single input: ai_router/changelog.d/0110-set-129-suite-owned-input-sets.md, a markdown fragment. A close-out changelog entry under ai_router/ arms a 6.5-minute browser suite, and that is the stronger covers definition binding its own author on the very session that wrote it down: cost is a reason to make a suite cheaper, never a reason to declare an input set smaller than it is. npm run compile regenerated no tracked dist/ drift, so the pytest run recorded before it stayed fresh.
